decision: Measure the test-studio tab cliff in one Chromium context, then commit a test of that stall, then two reviewed design notes
why: The Slack report says latest Studio stops loading around 8 tabs with Sanity requests stuck Pending. A cross-tab share is a one-way design, so the run measures first and does not ship an architecture.

decision: Ten structure tabs stayed up. Each held 5 listen streams and a ping still returned in under 10ms.
why: The API allows 100 HTTP/2 streams, so 5 streams per tab predicts a stall near 20 tabs, not 8. Bundled dev crashed this VM, so the run used classic Vite.

decision: Sixteen structure tabs stayed up. Tab 16 held 5 HTTP/2 listens and a ping returned 200 in 12ms. The run stopped while opening tab 17 because Chrome RSS was about 10GB.
why: floor(100/5) predicts a stall near 20 structure tabs. Memory stopped the run before the API cap.

decision: Replaying listen fetches without reading the body stalled the next listen once 98 extra 200 responses were held. The ping at 95 held returned 200 in 655ms.
why: 204 listen responses complete. 200 responses hold the stream. The probe saw one HTTP/2 connection.

decision: The hermetic script queued the next fetch at 6 HTTP/1.1 connections and at HTTP/2 cap 100, then recovered after one EventSource close.
why: This is the Pending mechanism. The script does not start Studio and does not need a token.

decision: unstable_bundledDev stays true. A local false flip let classic Vite load on this VM and was not committed.
why: Bundled dev threw requestLazy is not a function during page load. That crash is separate from the tab stall.
